name: Victorian architectural terracotta
summary: Fired clay blocks in buff, red and blue-grey that English makers pressed in moulds for museums, schools and town halls. Cheap in a smoky city, the clay kept its colour where stone turned black.

philosophy.core_thesis: A smoky industrial city needs a facade that rain can wash: a glazed or hard-fired clay block gives rich ornament at a price that a mason cannot meet.
design_principles: Press the ornament in plaster moulds, so that one design repeats across a whole facade.
Make each block hollow, with webs inside, 25 to 50 mm thick, so that it dries and fires without a crack.
Use one colour for the main wall and a second for the band, the arch and the frieze.
Model plant and animal forms in high relief: leaves, birds, fruit, beasts and Romanesque arches.
Fire the blocks at a high heat until the clay is hard and does not take soot.
Hang the blocks on a brick or iron frame with iron cramps and fill the cavity with mortar.
Add a glaze or a coloured slip for the bands that need to wash clean in the rain.
anti_patterns: A smooth cast concrete facade with no moulded ornament
Blocks that vary in colour from one firing to the next
A carved stone detail that a mason cuts one by one
Thin, flat panels with no relief
A shiny, even glaze over the whole wall

form.shape: Facade blocks, string courses, window surrounds, columns, capitals, finials, chimney pots and big relief panels for friezes.
form.profile: A deep relief with a sharp edge and a strong shadow; arches are round or pointed, and the leaves stand out 3 to 8 cm from the ground.
form.foot_and_rim: Each block is hollow and open at the back; the face has a sharp arris and the edges are straight so that the joints stay thin.
form.proportion: A block is about 30 to 60 cm long and 15 to 30 cm high; the wall of the block is 25 to 50 mm thick.
rules: Make each block hollow with internal webs.
Repeat the mould for the same motif.
Use two clay colours in bands.
Give each block a number for its place on the plan.

bodies.rule: Blend several clays and a grog of ground fired clay, so that the body presses cleanly and fires hard with little shrinkage. Keep the colour even in each batch.

forming.joins: Blocks are bedded in lime or cement mortar on a brick backing and tied with iron cramps; joints are 3 to 6 mm thin.
forming.details: A mould seam on the back, a maker stamp in the body, and a number or letter that marks the place of the block.

glaze.pattern: Rows of leaves, flowers, birds and beasts in high relief; bands of tiles and plain panels in buff and red, with a blue-grey for the arch.
glaze.gloss: Matt for the bare body, about 5 to 20 GU; glazed bands reach 60 to 85 GU.
glaze.wear: The bare body keeps its edge but takes a dark patina in a city; glazed parts wash clean in the rain.

palette.strategy: Warm buff, brick red and a cool blue-grey in large flat fields; a few glazed bands in turquoise, green or cream give a bright accent.

firing.kiln: A muffle or downdraught kiln fired with coal; the blocks stand on edge in saggars, so that the flame does not touch the face.
processes: drying for one to two weeks
a second glaze firing for glazed parts
firing.scale: Large works in Lambeth, Leeds and Stoke supplied whole museums, schools, banks and town halls; one building used thousands of blocks.
firing.signs: A maker stamp on the back, a thin mould seam and a slight colour change between kiln loads.

pieces.form: Hollow facade block with a moulded leaf and a bird in a round arch
Frieze panel with a row of beasts and plants
Column capital with a leaf spray and a ring of fruit
Tall chimney pot with a moulded and incised twist
Glazed band with a raised flower on a cream ground

positive: high relief leaf and bird panels
museum or school front in warm clay

emotion.target_response: Civic pride and richness: the viewer sees a public building that wears its ornament as a sign of progress.

use_cases: a heritage or conservation brief on a terracotta facade
a render of a Victorian public building
a label on a moulded terracotta frieze
avoid_when: the brief needs a glossy white wall
the brief needs a flat curtain wall
the brief needs a natural stone surface

modifiers.how: Change to a steel frame with thin terracotta cladding in a cream colour and flat, organic ornament.
Remove the ornament, extrude hollow panels with a matt face, and hang them on rails with an air gap.

ornament_level.note: Ornament is the point of the style; keep it above 0.5 for a true Victorian facade.

wall_thickness.note: A hollow block has a wall of 25 to 50 mm; the knob stops at 40 mm.
